Initially planned as a 3-month intervention beginning September 2021, WFP faced numerous challenges that necessitated the exten-sion of the project to ensure the delivery of needed fuel quantities to targeted WASH facilities. The challenges included:
• Lack of data availability and accuracy for the identification of facilities
• Oversupply of fuel as a number of facilities were receiving diesel through sources other than WFP
• Sporadic security incidents and harsh weather conditions that hindered the delivery of fuel

Fuel
The below graph showcases the variation of fuel deliveries in-line with the increase of international fuel prices
WFP had initially planned to deliver a total of 6 million litres of fuel (at 57 cents/litre) to WASH facilities to ensure continuity of their operation. International fuel prices however increased be-tween August 2021 and February 2022 from 57 cents per litre to a record high of 74 cents per litre respectively. This meant that the final distribution target had to be revised in-line with availa-ble funding resources at an average of 64 cents/litres during the intervention.
• At 57 cents/litre: possible delivery of 6 million litres of fuel
• At 64 cents/litre: actual delivery of 5.3 million litres of fuel
